I believe the government should pursue providing all citizens a universal basic income (UBI) funded by higher taxes on the wealthy. This policy aligns with my values of equity, dignity, and economic security. UBI would provide a financial safety net for everyone, reducing poverty and allowing individuals to pursue opportunities without the constant stress of survival. It recognizes the inherent dignity of all people by ensuring that basic needs are met, regardless of circumstances.

Higher taxes on the wealthy are a fair and necessary mechanism to fund this initiative. Wealth inequality has reached staggering levels, and those with the most resources have a moral obligation to contribute more to society. Progressive taxation would help redistribute wealth in a way that fosters greater economic stability and social cohesion. Critics argue that UBI could disincentivize work, but evidence from pilot programs suggests otherwise: people use the income to improve their lives, whether by investing in education, starting businesses, or caring for loved ones.

Moreover, UBI could simplify welfare systems, reducing bureaucratic inefficiencies and ensuring aid reaches those who need it most. In an era of automation and job displacement, UBI offers a proactive solution to economic insecurity. By prioritizing collective well-being over individual wealth accumulation, this policy reflects a commitment to justice and shared prosperity.
